text: The idea in one sentence: Raschka teaches position on one eight-word sentence: GPT-2 adds a position vector to each token once, RoPE instead rotates each pair of query and key numbers by its position so that a score depends only on how far apart two tokens are, and recent open models have started to rotate only part of each head, to skip RoPE in some layers, or (Inkling) to learn a bias on the score instead.

text: New terms: split-half and interleaved pairing (which two numbers of a head RoPE turns together: i with i + d/2, or neighbours); partial RoPE (only some pairs of each head are rotated); NoPE layer (a layer with no explicit position signal; the causal mask still orders tokens); learned relative position bias (a number added to each score before the softmax that depends on the distance between query and key).

text: Position can enter at five places in one layer, and the article walks through them in order One token through one attention layer (left), and where each scheme the article covers adds position (right). §2: added once to the input embedding (GPT-2's learned table, the 2017 sinusoids). §3 to 5: every pair of q and k rotated by position (full RoPE, used by most models). §6.1: only some pairs rotated (partial RoPE; MiniMax-M3 rotates 64 of each head's 128 numbers). §6.2: no rotation in this layer (a NoPE layer; SmolLM3 skips RoPE in every fourth of its 36 layers). §6.3: a learned bias by distance added to the score (Inkling; T5 did a simpler version in 2019).
